font.$description: Font stacks. The default is the platform UI stack: no network request, no font license to track.

sans.$value: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif

mono.$value: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

display.$description: Display and heading face. The declared stack is the platform fallback: no webfont ships in the default path, so a consumer replaces the whole stack in one line with a geometric or techno sans (Space Grotesk, Chakra Petch) by setting `--sk-font-display`. The arcade character comes from the weight and tracking on the display steps regardless of family.

text.$description: Type scale. Each token emits a shorthand pair: size / line-height.

display.$description: Display headings. Heavy weight, tight tracking.

space.$description: Spacing scale, rem-based so it honors the user's root font size.

height.$description: Control heights. Icon-only controls must still hit --sk-touch-min.

min.$description: 44px minimum hit target for every interactive element (WCAG 2.2 target size).

radius.$description: Corner radii. Chrome is nearly square: the house style is a hard-edged neo-brutalist surface, and 2-6px of rounding softens it without losing that character — a fully sharp corner reads as unfinished at control sizes, and a fully round one reads as a different library. `full` is a shape, not a style, for the badge dot and spinner. Glass overlays keep their own large radii so they read as a distinct material.

md.$description: Chrome radius. Matches Santaka-Pay rounded-pixel (10px): large enough to read as soft and intentional, small enough to stay hard-edged.

glass.$description: Floating overlays: dialog, popover, toast, tooltip, palette.

glass-lg.$description: Largest floating surface, such as the command palette.

border.$description: Two weights only. `width` is the hairline for separators and input fields; `thick` carries all brutalist chrome.

thick.$description: Chrome stroke. 2px, matched to Santaka-Pay control borders — the previous 3px on every element made the page vibrate; two weights stay (1px hairline, 2px chrome).

ring.$description: Focus ring geometry. A hard 3px stroke at 3px offset, not a soft glow.

shadow.$description: Hard offsets layered with an ambient blur. Geometry only, and deliberately so: the colour is consumed from --sk-shadow-color (opaque, hard layer) and --sk-shadow-ambient (translucent, blur), both defined per theme. A literal colour here would force one theme to override the whole ladder. A pure zero-blur offset is flat and disappears on a dark surface; Santaka-Pay pairs the same hard offset with a wide low-opacity shadow behind it, which makes a brutalist surface read as lifted rather than outlined.

glass.$description: The only alpha values in the system, which is what makes glass read as a distinct material. Every color here is theme-dependent and declared per theme, because a translucent panel has to track the theme's surface; only the effect values are shared.

duration.$description: Motion durations, split by layer. Interactive controls use short arcade timing; floating overlays use longer float timing. The reduced-motion override in styles/reset.css collapses these.

ease.$description: Easing curves, split by layer. `arcade` overshoots so the press visibly springs back; `glass` starts fast and settles long.

z.$description: Layer tokens. Components read these instead of hard-coding z-index.
